Thirty-five comments

The Colliers’ Reel

Source: Paddy Keenan: “Poirt an Phiobaire”
Transcription: g.m.p.

↳ Posted by gian marco on November 15th, 2003.

Collier’s Reel

I heard Eoin O’Riabhaigh play this one at the 2003 Tionol in Chapel Hill. Michael Vignoles also plays this one. A great tune!

↳ Posted by Matt McNeely on October 1st, 2004.

The Colliers

The version based on Paul O’Shaughnessy and Harry Bradley’s duet playing:

K: Dmix
FDFG A3B|cAdB cAGB|Add^c d2de|fde^c dcAG|
FDFG A3B|cAdB cAGB|Add^c ABAG|1 EFGE FDDE:|2 EFGE FDD2||
f2eg fde^c|Add^c Adde|f2eg fde^c|AGAB c3d|
eaag efge|dfed cAGB|Add^c ABAG|1 EFGE FDD2:|2 EFGE FDDE||

Some people might prefer starting the tune like this: |FD (3EFG A3B|….

This tune comes up in many of recent recordings, and so you’ll come across it several times in new places.

↳ Posted by slainte on July 25th, 2005.

Colliers’

This is a sweet little tune. I was listening to Tommy Peoples’ setting of it on “Waiting for a Call” this morning. Sounds to me like he is playing it down a 5th (Gmix). Really changes the feeling. I love it.

↳ Posted by RogueFiddler on September 12th, 2005.

Colliers

I love Tommy Peoples version too. However the tune as hear it has a second part to the second part which is not notated anywher I can find.
Can somebody give me the full setting, please!!!

↳ Posted by The Quiet Man on October 9th, 2006.

Colliers

I have found the full version in Tommy Peoples 50 Irish fiddle tunes in the key of Gmix but it’s still not quite as I hear it in he second part. I know Tommy has his unique phrasing but would be nice to get near it. My ear is not as good as I would like and therefore have to rely on written music to fill the blanks in. Ah well, maybe next lifetime!!

↳ Posted by The Quiet Man on October 14th, 2006.

↳ Posted by slainte on July 5th, 2007.

They have a couple of bars similar in the B-part, but how did you find out they were related to each other?

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on July 5th, 2007.

I think the relation between the two reels is a broad fact, which has already been pointed out by someone else. They share *basically* the same B-part. The thing is, the version Gian Marco transcribed isn’t very standard.

Dow, I know you will never agree with me on this, so let’s not talk about it any more. It actually doesn’t matter whether they are related or not, simply because they aren’t the same tune.

↳ Posted by BriarRose on January 8th, 2026.

Re: The Colliers’

Re. “Paahto’s” comment above [ 19 years ago ! ], I have just heard the recording he’s referring to. The “song”, which only has 2 very short verses, is called “Why She Could’t Drink Her Tea”, and features the reel played on flute, singing the 2 verses, and lilting. According to my source, it was recorded in 1926, on the Victor label, catalogue number 79015.
Eureka - it’s on Youtube :
https://youtu.be/IHAvch1VzWo?si=8UiSKL_TRWg-3fHp

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 12th, 2026.

Re: The Colliers’ / Why She Couldn’t drink her Tea / John Griffin

As an alternative to youtube, there’s an audio file for this excellent 1926 John Griffin recording that was mentioned above by Paahto and Kenny, here:
http://www.juneberry78s.com/sounds/ListenToIrishDance.htm
(I came across this recording while listening through this collection.)

The raw file is here:
https://www.juneberry78s.com/sounds/jgi78-01.mp3
There’s some valuable info on youtube, written no doubt by Dominic Keogh, the guy who put the recording up there. I may as well share it here:
>>
John Griffin, known as “The 5th Avenue Busman”, originally from the townland of Cloontowart in Lisacul, co Roscommon. More well known for recording comedic songs popular during the 20’s, John was also a very fine Flute player in the percussive and rhythmic style of his home. He emigrated to New York and made many recordings for various labels including Victor and Regal. Here he plays a version of the reel “The Colliers”.
